$comment: Exam form(s). v1 ships one form; schema is multi-form-ready. Built at S6 per .claude/skills/exam-publish by exam-examiner, 2026-08-18, on the S5 round-1 bank revision (questions.json commit 4090ed3; eval/ commit eacb373 — 121/122 blind, zero bounces, zero dimensions <=2). Selection method (methodology/02-master-inventory.md #priority + /exam-publish step 1): seat priority:high (convergent, sources>=2) concepts first, then fill to the manifest's per-domain format mix; reserves are substitutes, not rejects. This bank maps concepts 1:1 to items (122 items, 122 merged family-level concepts), so seating an item seats its concept. Arithmetic verified against the manifest: 90 items = d1 11 (10 SC + 1 MR + 0 SM) + d2 20 (17+2+1) + d3 16 (15+1+0) + d4 25 (21+3+1) + d5 18 (15+2+1); 81 of the 82 high-priority concepts seated + 9 normal-priority seats; 32 reserve-only concepts (= bank 122 - exam 90). STRUCTURAL NOTE: the bank holds exactly 9 multiple_response and 3 scenario_matching items and the exam mix asks for exactly 9 and 3, per domain — so every MR and SM item is force-seated and the only degrees of freedom are the 78 SC seats out of 110 SC bank items. HAND-ADJUSTMENTS (documented per skill): (1) d2 is the only over-subscribed domain — 18 high-priority SC concepts for 17 SC seats — so exactly one high is reserved: d2-q04 (C-019, naming a social-engineering attack from its message channel). It is the joint lowest-scoring d2 SC high (dim5=3, dim6=4: the stem's 'text messages' hands the channel over across a thin wrapper) and its outline group keeps d2-q05 (impersonation levels) and d2-q06 (indirect vectors: typosquatting, watering hole, misinformation) seated, so social engineering stays covered. First-line substitute for any d2 SC seat. (2) d1 needs no judgment: its 10 high-priority concepts are all single_choice and there are exactly 10 SC seats, and its one MR item d1-q08 (C-008, normal) is force-seated by the format mix — so all four d1 normals reserved (d1-q03, d1-q09, d1-q11, d1-q13) are SC. (3) The format mix forces three further normal-priority seats: d2-q25 (SM, C-037 indicator families) and d2-q27 (MR, C-042 lifecycle mitigations) are the only items of their format in d2. (4) Six normal-priority SC fills chosen for objective breadth and judged quality, each covering a blueprint bullet no seated high reaches: d3-q07 (C-049 IoT/ICS/SCADA/RTOS constraints - the whole 'infrastructure considerations' slice, uncovered otherwise), d3-q11 (C-053 port security, 802.1X/EAP - perfect 6x5 judge score), d3-q21 (C-063 the four plan-testing levels: tabletop, failover, simulation, parallel), d4-q19 (C-083 SPF/DKIM/DMARC - the only email-authentication coverage in the bank), d4-q24 (C-088 access control models MAC/DAC/RBAC/rule/ABAC - the blueprint-only concept Gate 1 spot-traced as Domain 4's largest single-objective gap), d5-q17 (C-115 compliance proven continuously: due diligence/due care, attestation and acknowledgement, automation - perfect 6x5, and the only form coverage of objective 5.4's compliance half, since seated d5-q18/q19 cover its privacy half). (5) Reserved normals with rationale: d3-q20 (C-062 continuity/capacity) and d3-q18 (C-060 access-side data protection) overlap seated d3-q19+d3-q22 (resilience) and seated d2-q22/q23 (segmentation, least privilege) respectively; d4-q30 (C-094 IR rehearsal: training/tabletop/simulation) is deliberately NOT seated alongside d3-q21, which tests the same exercise ladder - seating both would spend two of eight normal seats on one discrimination; d4-q05/q13/q21/q22 (asset inventory, post-alert handling, account lifecycle, password policy levers) all score 6x5 and are the top substitutes for any d4 SC seat; d5-q05 (C-103 risk identification and assessment cadence), d5-q02 (C-100 obligation scope) and d5-q22 (C-120 passive vs active recon) are the d5 substitutes in that order. (6) FLAGGED ITEMS AND THE FORM (read with derivation/gate2-checklist.md): 6 of the 14 Gate 2 sample items are seated - d1-q04, d1-q06, d2-q15 (dim5=3), d1-q10, d2-q13, d3-q15 (dim2=3). Three more are off the form structurally, not by choice: d2-q07, d2-q12, d2-q14 are d2 normals and d2 has zero normal SC seats. The remaining five were reserved on merit, each being the lowest-scoring candidate in the competition set it lost - d4-q02 (C-066 BYOD/COPE; sum 28, the lowest of the eleven d4 SC normals, AND the bank's one open blind-solve adjudication: seating an item whose key may change at Gate 2 would force a form rebuild, so it waits as first substitute pending Oliver's verdict), d5-q16 (dim1=3, the contested-best-answer flag; it competes for the same 5.4 compliance seat as the perfect-scoring d5-q17), d3-q08 and d3-q16 (both dim2=3 and both the joint lowest-scoring d3 normals; d3-q16's sovereignty/geolocation is additionally the narrowest bullet in a data-protection group that keeps d3-q14/q15/q17, and seated d5-q18 carries the legal-geography idea), and d2-q04 per adjustment 1. This does NOT dodge either Gate 2 policy question: the dim-5 vocabulary-recognition decision keeps 3 of its 5 instances on the form (including d2-q15, the clearest one) and the dim-2 throwaway-option decision keeps 3 of its 7. If Gate 2 accepts the flags, the five reserved items are substitutes in their domains; if Gate 2 bounces any of them, this form is unaffected.
